title: Importance of good citizenship
competency: Describe the importance of good citizenship and compare a community with and without it.

keywords.def: Living as a citizen who obeys the law, is responsible, tolerant and patriotic.
Respect that people show each other in both directions.
A respectful discussion between people with different views that helps find common ground.

en.text: Good citizenship builds a strong moral code and a safe, supportive society. A lasting democracy depends on it. It helps people with different views debate respectfully and find common ground. It builds mutual respect, so people work toward a common goal. When citizens challenge injustice and promote fairness, violence is reduced.

screens.title: Imagine a school…
screens.ask: What would happen in your school if students, teachers and leaders had no good citizenship?
opts: Rules would be broken and there would be conflict
screens.after: Without good citizenship there would be disorder, disrespect and conflict. Learning would suffer. Read why good citizenship matters.

screens.title: 1.1.3 Importance of good citizenship
paras: Good citizenship builds a strong moral code in individuals.
It fosters a safe and supportive society and keeps democracy alive.
It benefits the environment and makes our country a better place.
We are all responsible for building our country's strength.

screens.title: Respect and debate
paras: Good citizenship helps people with opposing views debate constructively.
It teaches students to find common ground with people who are different.
It builds mutual respect and understanding, so people work toward a common goal.
It helps students resist all forms of extremism.
screens.note: Remember: mutual respect and understanding are fostered by good citizenship character.

screens.title: Fairness
paras: A good citizen challenges injustice and promotes fairness.
For example, a person may tell the authorities about a theft in the neighbourhood.
This keeps communities safe and the justice system fair.
When everyone promotes fairness, violence is reduced.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Respect that people show each other in both directions.
A respectful discussion between people with different views that helps find common ground.

screens.why: The Remember box says this directly.

screens.text: Tap the benefits of good citizenship from the book.
pool: Making our country a better place
a: Making our country a better place
screens.why: All of these are in the book's list except more violence; good citizenship reduces violence.
screens.clue: One option is a harm, not a benefit.

screens.text: What would you do if you saw a student tearing up papers and throwing them in your classroom?
opts: Politely ask the student to stop and use the bin; tell the teacher if it continues
screens.ans: Politely ask the student to stop and use the bin; tell the teacher if it continues
screens.why: Keeping the environment clean and reporting wrongdoing are responsibilities of a good citizen.
screens.clue: What are a good citizen's responsibilities?

screens.text: A healthy and long-lasting democratic society depends on good citizenship.
Two groups in a woreda argue about where to build a new well. Which response shows good citizenship best?
opts: Hold a respectful debate, listen to both sides and find common ground
screens.ans: Hold a respectful debate, listen to both sides and find common ground
screens.why: Good citizenship fosters constructive debate and finding common ground toward a common goal.

items.text: Without good citizenship, what relationship would exist between students, teachers and administrators?
items.why: Good citizenship builds respect and cooperation; without it these are lost.

items.text: Figure 1.8 shows students debating. What does it represent?
opts: Good citizenship lets people with different views discuss respectfully
items.ans: Good citizenship lets people with different views discuss respectfully
items.why: The book says good citizenship fosters constructive debate.

items.text: By carrying out your responsibilities, can you have a positive impact on your community?
opts: Yes: I help build a safe, supportive community and a better country
items.ans: Yes: I help build a safe, supportive community and a better country
items.why: The book says we are all responsible for building our country's strength.

test.text: Good citizenship reduces violence based on religious, linguistic or ethnic differences.
test.why: When people respect and care for each other, such violence is reduced.

test.text: Telling the authorities about a theft in the neighbourhood helps to…
opts: keep communities safe and justice fair
test.ans: keep communities safe and justice fair
test.why: The book gives this example of challenging injustice.

test.text: Good citizenship teaches students to find ___ with people who are different.
Which is NOT an importance of good citizenship?
test.why: Good citizenship helps students resist extremism.

test.text: A school where students respect each other and report wrongdoing will most likely be…
test.why: Good citizenship fosters a safe and supportive society.
